content.value: A TypeScript SDK monorepo for consuming Barkpark from JavaScript and Next.js — the client layer beneath the Web Demo.
The JS SDK is a TypeScript monorepo living in

, one of the Surfaces that front Barkpark. Where the Go TUI and bp CLI target the terminal, the JS SDK targets browser and Node runtimes, giving JavaScript and Next.js apps a typed way to read and write content over HTTP API v1.

Responses come back wrapped in a stable envelope — a consistent shape carrying the payload alongside metadata — so callers parse results uniformly regardless of which endpoint they hit. The SDK turns a Document fetch, a Mutation write, or a Search query into typed calls, with Auth and Tokens handled for the consumer. Writes are still validated server-side against Schema v2.

The SDK's primary consumer is the Web Demo — the Next.js finder on barkpark.cloud — which leans on it to drive the master/detail finder backed by the Indx Engine. The SDK also gives apps a clean seat to receive Webhooks for Cache Revalidation, so a content change in LiveView Studio or via the bp CLI can invalidate cached pages downstream.

Like the other clients, an SDK consumer can read the Capabilities Manifest to learn which Plugins verbs and endpoints the server currently offers, keeping the JS layer aligned with whatever Phoenix API is running.
